{"id": "ac60e9e1-8479-41a2-bc9f-3f1b8626c707", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "The error text usually tells you which case you're in. Often it is fixable in IAM, but not always.

## Read the error message first
The text after "AccessDeniedException" separates the causes:

| Message says | Cause | Where to fix it |
|---|---|---|
| "...no identity-based policy allows the bedrock:InvokeModel action" | The role has no Allow for the action or resource. | Your IAM policy |
| "...with an explicit deny in an identity-based policy" | A Deny statement is matching. | Your IAM policy |
| "...not authorized to perform the required AWS Marketplace actions (aws-marketplace:ViewSubscriptions, aws-marketplace:Subscribe)" | The first call to a third-party model tries to auto-subscribe through AWS Marketplace, and the role can't do that. | IAM permissions on the role, or an admin activates the model once for the account |
| "...with an explicit deny in a service control policy" (or a permissions boundary or session policy) | Something outside the role's own policy is blocking the call. | AWS Organizations or your platform team, not your IAM policy |

## Causes that look like an IAM problem but have a different fix
- **Inference profiles:** Some models can only be invoked through a cross-Region inference profile. If your policy only allows `arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/<model-id>`, calls made through a profile fail. Add the `arn:aws:bedrock:*::inference-profile/<profile-id>` ARN to `Resource`.
- **Marketplace activation:** Once an admin with the Marketplace permissions invokes the model once, any role in the account can use it. A new subscription can take up to about 2 minutes to take effect, and you may keep seeing the error during that time. Amazon, Meta, Mistral, DeepSeek, Qwen and OpenAI models don't need Marketplace permissions.
- **Organization guardrails:** If an SCP or permissions boundary blocks Bedrock or a Region, no change to your role's policy will fix it. Someone with access to the Organization has to adjust it.

## A policy to start from
```json
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["bedrock:InvokeModel", "bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream"],
  "Resource": [
    "arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/<model-id>",
    "arn:aws:bedrock:*::inference-profile/<profile-id>"
  ]
}
```
For a third-party model's first invocation, the role also needs `aws-marketplace:ViewSubscriptions` and `aws-marketplace:Subscribe`. `aws-marketplace:Unsubscribe` appears in the same AWS troubleshooting guidance.

## What I need from you
If you paste the full error message, I can tell you which case it is. I'd also need the model ID, or the inference profile ID if you use one, the Region, and the role or user your app runs as. With the role and Region, I can check the role's attached policies and boundary in your account. I can also look for SCP restrictions if the account is associated with this space.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
